```{r, include = FALSE}
source("_setup.R")
```

FragPipe writes different tables for label-free and for TMT experiments; DiffPTM reads both.

## Label-free (IonQuant)

| Table | File | Columns DiffPTM reads |
|---|---|---|
| total proteome | `combined_protein.tsv` of the proteome workflow | `Protein ID`, `Gene`, `<sample> MaxLFQ Intensity` (preferred) or `<sample> Intensity` |
| PTM | `combined_modified_peptide.tsv` of the enrichment workflow (LFQ-phospho, ...) | `Protein ID`, `Gene`, `Peptide Sequence`, `Modified Sequence`, `Assigned Modifications`, `Start`, `Probability`, `<sample> MaxLFQ Intensity` |

Sites are read from `Assigned Modifications` (`5S(79.9663), 9T(79.9663)`: positions within
the peptide, converted to protein positions with `Start`); fixed and label modifications
(57.0215, 15.9949, 42.0106, 229.1629, 304.2071) are ignored. Several peptidoforms can carry the
same site (missed cleavages, additional modifications): *Collapse peptidoforms to sites* in
the processing step sums them.

The sample names are the experiment names given in the FragPipe workflow (`control_1`, ...).
When the enriched and proteome runs were run in two separate workflows with the same
experiment names, nothing needs renaming.

## TMT (TMT-Integrator)

| Table | File | Columns DiffPTM reads |
|---|---|---|
| total proteome | `abundance_protein_MD.tsv` (or `_None.tsv`, `_GN.tsv`) | `Index` / `ProteinID`, samples |
| PTM | `abundance_single-site_MD.tsv` (or `_None.tsv`) | `Index` (`P12345_S123`), `Gene`, `ProteinID`, `Peptide`, `MaxPepProb`, samples |

TMT-Integrator reports **log2 ratios to the reference channel plus the reference intensity**,
i.e. values already on the log2 scale: untick *Intensities are raw* in the import step
(`log2_transform = FALSE` in R). DiffPTM warns when values never exceed 64 and skips the
transformation. The sample names are the channel annotations of the TMT-Integrator
annotation file. Give the plex of each sample in the `mixture` column of the design; the
single model then fits one mixture effect per fraction.

The example files `inst/extdata/formats/FragPipe_LFQ/` and `FragPipe_TMT/` reproduce the two
layouts.

## In the interface

1. **Import**: software *FragPipe*; upload the two tables; untick *Intensities are raw* for
   TMT-Integrator tables.
2. **Design**: *Pre-fill from sample names* (condition = `-1`); for TMT fill the `mixture`
   column.
3. **Processing**: defaults; tick *Collapse peptidoforms to sites* for
   `combined_modified_peptide.tsv`.
4. **Statistics**, **Results**, **Download** as in the overview vignette.

## The same analysis in R, label-free

```{r lfq}
library(DiffPTM)
prot <- import_protein(fx("FragPipe_LFQ", "combined_protein.tsv"), "FragPipe")
ptm  <- import_ptm(fx("FragPipe_LFQ", "combined_modified_peptide.tsv"), "FragPipe")
head(ptm$meta[, c("feature_id", "label", "stripped_sequence", "residue", "position", "localization_prob", "ptm_type")])
ann <- guess_annotation(colnames(prot$intensity), "[_]", condition_pos = "-1")
x <- new_ptm_experiment(prot, ptm, annotation = list(protein = ann, ptm = ann)) |>
  filter_localization(0.75) |> filter_min_observed(min_n = 2) |>
  normalise(method = "global_median") |> match_ptm_to_protein("id")
res <- run_methods(x, make_contrasts(x, "vs_reference", reference = "control"), "limma", pi0_method = "bh")
table(res$analysis, significant = res$adj_pvalue < 0.05)
```

## The same analysis in R, TMT

```{r tmt}
prot <- import_protein(fx("FragPipe_TMT", "abundance_protein_MD.tsv"), "FragPipe", log2_transform = FALSE)
ptm  <- import_ptm(fx("FragPipe_TMT", "abundance_single-site_MD.tsv"), "FragPipe", log2_transform = FALSE)
range(prot$intensity, na.rm = TRUE)          # log2 scale already
ann <- guess_annotation(colnames(prot$intensity), "[_]", condition_pos = "-1")
ann$mixture <- "plex1"                      # one 6-plex here; give the plex of each channel in a multi-plex design
x <- new_ptm_experiment(prot, ptm, annotation = list(protein = ann, ptm = ann)) |>
  filter_localization(0.75) |> filter_min_observed(min_n = 2) |>
  normalise(method = "global_median") |> match_ptm_to_protein("id")
res <- run_methods(x, make_contrasts(x, "vs_reference", reference = "control"), "limma", pi0_method = "bh")
res$label <- x$ptm$meta$label[match(res$feature_id, x$ptm$meta$feature_id)]
table(res$analysis, significant = res$adj_pvalue < 0.05)
```

```{r volcano, fig.height = 5}
plot_volcano(subset(res, analysis == "ptm_DPU"), fdr = 0.05, title = "PTM usage, treated vs control (TMT)")
```

Global median normalisation (every channel centred on the same median) is the usual choice
for TMT ratios; per-condition centering assumes that most sites do not change between
conditions within a plex.
